label: copy-phase input n, mid-sequence (recall positions 2-4, near end)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the fed-back input token is n (99.98% of activations, essentially all mass); never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Within copy-phase n inputs (~38% of which are active) firing is gated by position: concentrated at recall_idx 2-4 (i.e. the n being re-input is original token 1-3) and when few outputs remain (to_go <= 4), so short sequences (L 3-6) dominate; n at recall_idx 1 or in long sequences with many outputs left is mostly inactive. Strongest activations are n as original token 1 in L=4-5 sequences (e.g. a n u c <DEL> a [n]); a second n right after the first activates more weakly. Simple n-in-copy-phase gets recall ~1.0 but precision 0.38; the positional window raises dev F1 to 0.79 (mass recall 0.91).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, u, -, f, w, e; least: 2, d, x, z) and the token being output (most: n, 0, c, e, w, u; least: p, b, 3, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=3.
